self_caught: Checker false-verdict (F7): greek_mech_entity.py's family-5 licenser test reported licenser=False for greek-out-entity-e4.md L162 «- Δεν έχω δει πώς εμφανίζεται το όνομα σε καμία επιφάνεια πέρα από τις 12 του φύλλου.» The regex matched only lower-case «δεν» and Greek does not case-fold under grep, so the sentence-initial «Δεν» was missed. Grading rule declared and applied uniformly, because it decided three verdicts: figures stated in an expectation's MAIN clause are required (e1.1 address/phone denominators, e2.1 '22 distinct third-party domains', e3.1 the three panel-status queries → FAIL when absent); figures inside a parenthetical gloss are not (e2.5 '16 positive, 7 neutral, 1 negative', e4.1 the per-form counts, e3.2 the trade-press parenthetical → PASS when the operative clause is met). Recorded so the coordinator can overturn it wholesale if the suite intends otherwise.
eval_feedback: e1.1, e2.1, e3.1 and e3.5 each bundle four to six separately-checkable figures into one expectation, so an output that gets the substance right and omits a single denominator is unrepresentable as anything but FAIL. Splitting 'population arithmetic' from 'surface-by-surface reporting' would make the grade informative instead of all-or-nothing.

The suite mixes required figures and illustrative figures without marking which is which. e2.1's '22 distinct third-party domains in all' sits in the main clause; e2.5's '(16 positive, 7 neutral, 1 negative)' sits in a parenthesis; e4.1's per-form counts sit in a parenthesis. A grader has to invent the rule (this run declared one — see self_caught). Mark mandatory figures explicitly.

e2.5 requires the correction to be made 'against the ΓΕΜΗ incorporation date of 14/03/2019', but that date lives in entity-profiles-inventory-pharos.md, which is NOT in eval 2's files list (only the mention log is). e2.6 simultaneously requires every date to trace to 'the log'. Literal satisfaction of e2.5 would violate e2.6. Fix by adding the inventory to eval 2's files or rewording to 'against the company's registry incorporation date'.

e1.5's 'any CORE-EEAT or CITE score are reported as not evaluated' does not say whether an explicit 'no score computed' sentence is required, or whether producing no score and marking the data-dependent CITE items unscoreable suffices. Both readings are live; this run took the second.

e4.4's 'one date and number convention used consistently' does not define 'number convention'. Digits-vs-spelled-out alternation for the same quantity is neither clearly in nor clearly out, and Greek business prose legitimately mixes them.

e3.4's 'and, if warranted, the Requested Articles process' is conditional, so it is unclear whether naming that specific Wikipedia mechanism is required or whether an equivalent 'independent editor, no relationship to the company' route passes.

e5.3 bundles four distinct asks — the SKILL.md six-type intake list, the three user-run checks, the capture date, and a locale/device refinement — and marks only the last as pass-either-way. The capture-date leg is easy to miss precisely because it is the fourth item in a long sentence; consider promoting it to its own expectation, since it is the one the expectation calls 'required'.

e1.1 and e4.1 both offer the 9-vs-8 name-string folding allowance, which worked well: it is the clearest example in the suite of an expectation that accepts two correct answers when the rule is stated. Worth copying to the address/phone/domain population counts.
